claims.summary:
The release is in output/release.json.

The earlier public releases (one of p0-p3 in the old epoch, none for p4, two of p0-p3 now) and the one-change bound leave six possible current datasets: 3, 5, 6, 9, 10 and 12. high (p0, p1 through both aliases, p4; utility 5), medium (4) and cross (3) are all authorized: p0's later consent revision supersedes the old denial. The partner sees the package ID, so I evaluate the whole policy. The previous per-world selector picked medium for worlds 3 and 12, and each of those outputs identified a single dataset. The best safe policy is cross, high, high, high, high, cross, with total utility 26. Every assigned package meets the guarantee of 3, and each output group varies p0, p1 and p2. This period's publication is cross with cross-count 1 and utility 3; two datasets share that output. The static medium policy is safe but only totals 24.

Code changes: partner_export/policy.py now runs a cover search over safe output groups in place of the per-world choice. tests/test_policy_regression.py covers the customer release, group safety, independence from the actual snapshot, guarantee changes, consent withdrawal, earlier releases and replayed or reordered records.
